definitions.K11_vs_paper_K14: K11 = paper K14 minus ['logreg_all_kv', 'gbm_all_kv', 'logreg_colour_kv'] (not in rescore files)
definitions.agreement: Spearman (Pearson on average ranks) of per-method mean scores between two datasets over a method set
definitions.summaries: wound pairs = mean of 6 wound-pair agreements; colonoscopy pairs = mean of 10; modality_diff = mean same-modality (16) minus mean across-modality (39) over the 11 references
definitions.method_bootstrap: methods resampled with replacement within the group, B 2000, default_rng(0), stats_v5/v7 design; same draws for every condition of a group; 95% percentile interval
definitions.grid_dice: dice(postprocess_prob(p, g), gt): the P0 pipeline (Gaussian sigma 2 smoothing, threshold g, components < 0.05% of frame removed) at each grid threshold; Dice only

variants.P0: postprocess_prob(p, t): Gaussian smoothing + threshold + small-component removal (main results)
variants.P1: postprocess(p >= t): closing then opening with 5 px ellipse, small-component removal

definitions.nsd: NSD at 1, 2, 3, 5 px and at 1% of the image diagonal; nsd2 is the paper's NSD
definitions.exclusions: results/exclusions_v5.json; fuseg_r256 uses the fuseg exclusions by index

alignment.note: every rescore file: same n and gt_empty as results/perimage32 for its set (fuseg_r256 vs fuseg), gt_fraction equal to 1e-9 except fuseg_r256 (resampled masks)

heldout.source: results/kaggle2/nnunet_heldout.json (FUSeg training images 400-549 minus duplicates; nnU-Net trained on images 0-392 minus duplicates, threshold fixed 0.5, P0)

_bottom_auto: Verdict: post-processing, NSD tolerance and resolution do not change either conclusion. The threshold protocol does change the size of the first one: a single common threshold for all models raises wound-pair agreement among modern methods, while removing calibration differences (per-dataset oracle threshold) lowers it.

- Wound-pair agreement among modern methods (M19) stays in the range of the main results under every post-processing variant, NSD tolerance, the resampled FUSeg, and the oracle threshold: Dice 0.122 to 0.262, NSD 0.317 to 0.522 (main results: Dice 0.211, NSD 0.473). No change from the main-result setting has a paired 95% interval that excludes 0.

- Exception, one common threshold: M19 wound-pair Dice agreement rises with the threshold, and the rise over the default is above 0 for every common threshold from 0.45 to 0.90. At 0.50 it is 0.412 [0.141, 0.646] (change 0.200 [0.035, 0.348]); the maximum is 0.621 at 0.90. For K11 no common threshold raises it (largest 0.182).

- Why: the mean Spearman between M19 method means on the wound sets and each method's FUSeg-tuned threshold is 0.27 at default thresholds, 0.55 at a common 0.50 and 0.57 at 0.90. This is consistent with the shared ranking at a high common threshold following how confident each model's probabilities are, a model trait that carries across datasets, rather than the datasets agreeing on which model segments wounds best. With each model's best threshold per dataset the agreement falls to 0.122 (K11 0.114).

- Modality structure: the modality difference stays above 0 in all 72 conditions for both M19 and K11 (lowest lower bound 0.007, thr common K11|0.65). Estimates range 0.185 to 0.455 (M19) and 0.245 to 0.615 (K11). The pooled sets with untrained or from-scratch methods are not in the rescore files and are not tested here.
- Post-processing barely reorders methods in Dice (lowest variant-to-variant rank correlation on a non-floor set: M19 0.900), but more in NSD (M19 0.726 on co2wounds; medetec 0.830).

- Resolution: resampling FUSeg to 256 px shifts M19 Dice by -0.017 and NSD by +0.166 on average (a fixed pixel tolerance is looser at lower resolution); the method ranking on FUSeg changes more for NSD (rank rho 0.682) than for Dice (0.918).

- MedSAM: official preprocessing changes MedSAM's reference-box Dice a lot, in both directions (-0.253 to +0.352; interval excludes 0 on 9 of 12 sets). Prompting with nnU-Net boxes beats nnU-Net in Dice only for SAM on ph2; in NSD only for SAM on azh, azh_train_slice; MedSAM with nnU-Net boxes on no set.
- Images without an nnU-Net box (prediction empty, scored 0 on a non-empty reference): 1 to 35 of 564 wound images and 0 to 581 of 690 colonoscopy images (exact only for empty references).
- nnU-Net on held-out FUSeg training images: Dice 0.8328 (n 148) vs 0.7943 on the FUSeg test set (n 112); difference +0.0385, interval [-0.024, +0.105].
